inputs.text: Chief Minister M.K. Stalin and the DMK are pushing ahead with their new manifesto packed full of big-government welfare handouts that erode personal responsibility and the traditional family unit. They plan to double women's monthly aid to Rs 2,000 while handing out Rs 8,000 household coupons, pulling people further from relying on their own families and communities and toward permanent state dependence. Farmers are being promised free motor pumpsets as one more handout designed to weaken the self-reliance that has always defined our rural way of life. The rest of their talk about FDI growth, job creation, extra support for fishermen, and a focus on AI development amounts to the same empty progressive promises we have heard before, all aimed at expanding government power at the expense of national strength and cultural continuity.
